Mount Cameroon.value: a considerable proportion of the 80 species of Alucitidae known from the Afrotropical region prior to this study
high diversity in many taxa, including other Lepidoptera groups
at the confluence of the Guinean and Congolian biogeographic regions
of diverse habitats along its elevational and precipitation gradients
surpasses expectations based on combinations of these exceptional factors in other Afrotropical localities
24 of these species have been described solely from the Mount Cameroon area

Bamboo Camp.value: a lowland rainforest with historical disturbances from selective logging.

Bimbia-Bonadikombo.value: a littoral forest in the part of the community forest that is officially disturbance-free, but with extensive current logging (Ferenc et al., 2018).

Crater Lake.value: a submontane rainforest locally disturbed by forest elephants.

Drink Gari.value: a lowland rainforest with a dense canopy layer.

Elephant Camp.value: a montane forest with a sparse canopy layer as a consequence of natural disturbances by forest elephants.

Mann’s Spring.value: a montane forest at the natural timberline.

Mapanja.value: a montane forest with mostly closed canopy layer.

PlanteCam.value: an upland rainforest in the transition between the lowland and montane zones, with a sparse canopy layer as a consequence of natural disturbance by forest elephants (Maicher et al. 2020b).
